paragraph: [Eutelsat secured a 15-year licence for its OneWeb low-earth-orbit service in Angola in 2025](<https://techafricanews.com/2025/06/30/eutelsat-group-secures-15-year-license-to-operate-oneweb-leo-connectivity-in-angola/>). In the last twelve months, [Q-KON and SISTEC opened a Luanda point of presence for Twoobii OneWeb in October 2026](<https://cajnewsafrica.com/2026/10/14/q-kon-sistec-launch-sovereign-satellite-service-for-angola/>). [In July 2026 the regulator, INACOM, licensed the startup NomaTech to sell internet access over ANGOSAT-2](<https://angop.ao/noticias/tecnologia/startup-do-moxico-recebe-licenca-para-fornecer-internet-via-angosat-2/>). No source found says services on two different satellite networks are on sale, and no sale over ANGOSAT-2 has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[MyBroadband's table lists Burundi as 'Available' for Starlink on 17 July 2026](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [Connecting Africa reports that Starlink launched services in Burundi in September 2024](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/unreliable-connectivity-impacts-burundi-s-citizens>). [Le360 lists Burundi among 29 African countries where Starlink had been granted a licence as of May 2026](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). In the last twelve months, [Community Voice named Starlink and NT Global as the satellite providers in March 2026](<https://communityvoice.bi/burundi-embarks-on-a-full-digitalization-journey/>). No source found names the network NT Global sells. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[ARCEP Benin lists Starlink among the operators with fixed internet subscriptions, with 2,550 subscriptions at 31 March 2026](<https://arcep.bj/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Observatoire_Internet_T1_2026_TaB.pdf>). [MyBroadband's Starlink status table of 17 July 2026 lists Benin as 'Available' for Starlink (SpaceX)](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, the regulator's Starlink count rose from [2,215 at Q4 2025](<https://arcep.bj/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/Observatoire_Internet_T1_2026_TaB.pdf>) to 2,550 at 31 March 2026. No source found says services on two different satellite networks are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[MyBroadband's status table of 17 July 2026 lists Burkina Faso with estimated Starlink availability '2026', not 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [The Minister of Digital Transition said negotiations with Starlink are advancing and the state hopes soon to decide whether to let it offer services](<https://www.queenmafa.net/2026/07/26/chantier-zero-donnee-a-lexterieur-120-plateformes-deja-repertoriees/>), so no authorisation has yet been given. [ARCEP recalled in March 2024 that Starlink held no authorisation](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[ITWeb, citing Ookla data for the first quarter of 2026, reports that Starlink is in service in Botswana](<https://itweb.africa/article/starlink-drives-african-broadband-speeds-higher/GxwQD71DnGyvlPVo>). [Paratus Botswana, in a company press release, says it provides Eutelsat low-earth-orbit (OneWeb) satellite services combined with terrestrial links to mining operations in Botswana](<https://itweb.africa/article/paratus-botswana-eutelsat-showcase-resilient-connectivity-and-redefine-how-mining-connects-in-southern-africa/lLn14MmQeANMJ6Aa>). [MyBroadband's table lists Botswana as Available on 17 July 2026](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

[ARCEP's half-year 2026 observatory says Starlink CAR obtained a licence to market and operate satellite fixed wireless internet, with no licence date](<https://www.icasees.org/index.php/component/edocman/observatoire-des-marches-de-communications-electroniques-s1-2027/download?Itemid=0>). [A table dated 17 July 2026 lists Starlink in the Central African Republic as 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, [a Ministry communiqué issued in Bangui in April 2026 suspended illegally imported Starlink kits operating in roaming mode](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/04/28/central-african-republic-suspends-starlink-kits-citing-security-and-equipment-traceability-requirements/>). No source found says a second satellite network is on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Starlink, sold directly to households, and Eutelsat Konnect, sold by Orange and MTN, are both on sale in Cote d'Ivoire as of the 28 July 2026 article](<https://tech-ish.com/2026/07/28/starlink-28-african-countries-kenya-freeze/>). [ARTCI authorised Starlink, subject to the regulator's ability to interrupt network access](<https://theconversation.com/faut-il-sinquieter-de-la-starlinkisation-de-lacces-a-internet-en-afrique-287464>). In the last twelve months, [MTN and Eutelsat made a Konnect capacity agreement in April 2026](<https://www.connectingafrica.com/connectivity/starlink-live-in-c-te-d-ivoire-and-seychelles>), beside Orange's existing Orange Sat service. No regulator's count of satellite broadband subscribers from the past three years has been found. Mature would need the regulator to publish the number of satellite broadband subscribers, from the past three years.

[NewsWatch reported on 27 July 2026 that Starlink's licence application in Cameroon had sat unresolved for over two years](<https://newswatchcameroon.com/cameroon-starlink-licensing-stalls-over-security-sovereignty-concerns/>). The regulator ART declined comment and said the file is with the ministry MINPOSTEL. [Cameroon is among 16 countries Starlink's availability map lists as 'Starting in 2026'](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3108-141168-internet-par-satellite-starlink-cible-16-nouveaux-marches-africains-d-ici-fin-2026>). In the last twelve months, [customs seized 10 Starlink modems at the Nkometou checkpoint on 12 December 2025 as unauthorised equipment](<https://actucameroun.com/2025/12/16/la-douane-saisit-des-kits-starlink-a-nkometou/>). Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[The regulator, ARPTC, licensed Starlink as an internet provider on 2 May 2025](<https://africa.businessinsider.com/local/markets/airtel-and-elon-musks-starlink-launch-africas-first-satellite-to-phone-service-in-drc/c3gcrdq>). [In March 2024 it had called the use of Starlink's network illegal](<https://actualite.cd/2025/05/02/rdc-starlink-obtient-une-licence-officielle-pour-operer-comme-fournisseur-dacces>). In the last twelve months, [Somaf Group opened a shop selling Starlink kits in Kindu in April 2026](<https://actualite.cd/2026/04/03/maniema-somaf-group-ouvre-un-bureau-kindu-et-mise-sur-starlink-pour-resorber-le-deficit>). [In July 2026 Radiocom, an authorised reseller, said Kinshasa's capacity on the residential plan was used up for four to six months](<https://www.talkafrica.co.ke/starlink-users-in-kinshasa-face-4-6-months-of-possible-slowdowns-amid-network-congestion/>). [The regulator's 2026 tariff page lists Konnect Africa with no tariff](<https://www.arptc-solution.cd/license_list/tarifview/1>), so no sale on a second network has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Le360 lists Congo-Brazzaville as 'available from 2026' with no licence granted to Starlink as of May 2026](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). [Agence Ecofin reports Congo is among 16 countries Starlink marks 'Starting in 2026' on its map, and that service was still not available despite a 2025 forecast](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3108-141168-internet-par-satellite-starlink-cible-16-nouveaux-marches-africains-d-ici-fin-2026>). [ARPCE seized an unauthorised Starlink installation in Congo-Brazzaville in June 2024](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[Al-Watwan reports that the regulator Anrtic announced a government ban on 12 June 2025, by ministerial circular signed 9 June 2025](<https://alwatwan.net/societe/d%C3%A9ploiement-de-starlink-i-les-autorit%C3%A9s-interdisent-son-usage-pour-l%E2%80%99instant.html>). The ban covers installing, testing, deploying or using Starlink, and no authorisation had been granted to Starlink. [Agence Ecofin reports that Starlink's availability map lists Comoros among 16 African countries marked 'Starting in 2026' with no launch date](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3108-141168-internet-par-satellite-starlink-cible-16-nouveaux-marches-africains-d-ici-fin-2026>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[The regulator ARME's market indicators for the second quarter of 2026 give Starlink 0.87 per cent of Cabo Verde's 500,263 internet access subscriptions](<https://expressodasilhas.cv/economia/2026/10/22/assinaturas-de-internet-fixa-aumentam-147-num-ano/105202>). [Starlink went live in Cape Verde in December 2024](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/08/05/cape-verde-opens-public-consultation-on-new-satellite-communications-regulatory-framework/>). In the last twelve months, its share rose from [0.64% of internet subscriptions in ARME's first-quarter 2026 report](<https://www.arme.cv/index.php/noticia-geral/1392-arme-publica-relatorio-indicadores-estatisticos-das-comunicacoes-eletronicas-1o-trimestre-de-2026>) to 0.87% at the end of June 2026. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Starlink's availability table of 17 July 2026 lists Djibouti as 'No planned launch date', so it is not on sale there](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [Le360 says Starlink's site gives Djibouti 'service date unknown'](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). [Djibouti is not in its list of 29 countries that had licensed Starlink as of May 2026](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). [Another article does not say whether any licence or application exists](<https://tech-ish.com/2026/07/28/starlink-28-african-countries-kenya-freeze/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[State-owned Algerie Telecom Satellite (VSAT and GMPCS licences) and Djezzy (VSAT licence) are the only companies authorised to provide satellite services in Algeria](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/1004-137437-services-telecoms-par-satellite-l-algerie-ouvre-la-porte-a-de-nouveaux-acteurs>). In the last twelve months, [ARPCE launched a call for competition on 9 April 2026 for two licences for public satellite networks in non-geostationary orbit](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/1004-137437-services-telecoms-par-satellite-l-algerie-ouvre-la-porte-a-de-nouveaux-acteurs>). [Algeria is listed among about 34 countries where Starlink is in regulatory limbo, as of June 2026](<https://cioafrica.co/namibia-shuts-the-door-on-starlink-twice/>). No source found says households or businesses can buy satellite broadband from a licensed provider. Establishing would need households or businesses able to buy satellite broadband from a licensed provider.

[Telegraph Egypt reported on 2025-06-18 that Starlink was not yet activated in Egypt](<https://www.egypttelegraph.com/article/154808/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%86%D8%AA-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%81%D8%B6%D8%A7%D8%A6%D9%8A-%D9%8A%D8%B7%D8%B1%D9%82-%D8%A3%D8%A8%D9%88%D8%A7%D8%A8-%D9%85%D8%B5%D8%B1-%D8%B3%D8%AA%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%84%D9%8A%D9%86%D9%83-%D8%AA%D9%86%D8%AA%D8%B8%D8%B1>). It said selling or marketing it requires an official licence not yet held, and talks with the ministry were under way. [A Starlink availability table lists Egypt as 'No planned launch date'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [Egypt is placed among countries in regulatory limbo for Starlink, neither approved nor explicitly banned](<https://cioafrica.co/namibia-shuts-the-door-on-starlink-twice/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[The Ethiopian Communications Authority stated in a public notice that Starlink has not been granted a licence in Ethiopia](<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/ethiopian-communications-authority_home-eca-activity-7346822754987393024-LHoH>). It said no discussions, past, ongoing or planned, have taken place with Starlink about one. [Birr Metrics reports that the Authority denied granting Starlink a licence](<https://birrmetrics.com/ethiopia-denies-granting-starlink-license-as-satellite-internet-expansion-faces-regulatory-pushback/>). [TechMag lists Ethiopia among countries that continue to block or restrict Starlink to protect state-owned telecoms](<https://technomag.co.zw/starlinks-african-expansion-availability-costs-and-performance/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[Gabon's regulator Arcep announced a ban on installing, using and marketing Starlink offers in Gabon, with prison and fines for offenders](<https://theconversation.com/faut-il-sinquieter-de-la-starlinkisation-de-lacces-a-internet-en-afrique-287464>). [Agence Ecofin reports Starlink's availability map shows Gabon as 'Starting in 2026', meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, and the service is still not available](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3108-141168-internet-par-satellite-starlink-cible-16-nouveaux-marches-africains-d-ici-fin-2026>). [Le360 lists Gabon among countries where Starlink is announced for 2026 with no licence granted](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[The NCA approved Starlink's application in April 2024](<https://nca.org.gh/2024/04/25/nca-approves-starlinks-satellitte-broadband-application/>), and [in August 2024 said Starlink would start operating by the end of that month](<https://nca.org.gh/2024/08/22/starlink-starts-operations-in-ghana-end-of-august-2024/>). [Its November 2024 guidance says customers can buy the Starlink kit online or from four resellers](<https://nca.org.gh/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/FAQs-Starlink-in-Ghana-1.pdf>). [The NCA counted 15,384 satellite internet subscriptions in June 2025](<https://www.itu.int/itu-d/meetings/wp-content/uploads/IPS/documents/35/35_ITU_EGTI2025_EmanuelNeizer_SatelliteBasedInternetConnectivityStatistics_GhanaExperience.pdf>). In the last twelve months it was cited and not changed: [MyBroadband listed Starlink as available in July 2026](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [The minister said in March 2024 that OneWeb was licensed](<https://capacityglobal.com/news/ghana-to-licence-starlink-in-response-to-subsea-cable-cuts/>), but no OneWeb sale has been found. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Agence Ecofin reported on 31 August 2026 that Guinea is among 16 countries marked 'Starting in 2026' on Starlink's availability map](<https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/3108-141168-internet-par-satellite-starlink-cible-16-nouveaux-marches-africains-d-ici-fin-2026>). Starlink service is still not available there. [MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table lists Guinea with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, [ARPT agents were reported on 10 August 2026 to be uninstalling and confiscating Starlink equipment used by Wi-Fi resellers](<https://theconversation.com/faut-il-sinquieter-de-la-starlinkisation-de-lacces-a-internet-en-afrique-287464>). Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[TechnoMag's article of 29 June 2026 lists the Gambia among 19 countries 'Scheduled for 2026', not among those where Starlink is active](<https://technomag.co.zw/starlinks-african-expansion-availability-costs-and-performance/>). [MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table lists Gambia with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, [the Minister of Digital Economy refused to approve the VSAT permit paid for in February 2026, saying Starlink needs a general satellite licence](<https://orbitaltoday.com/2026/05/24/starlink-licence-gets-delayed-by-the-gambia/>). Nothing dated later names a provider licensed. Preparing would need the regulator or ministry to have licensed a provider to sell internet over satellite in the country.

[MyBroadband's table lists Guinea-Bissau as 'Available' for Starlink as of 17 July 2026](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, [ARN-TIC, by Despacho 15/CA/ARN/2026, extended to 31 December 2026 the provisional General Authorisation held by Starlink Guiné-Bissau SARL](<https://arn.gw/comunicado-arn-tic/>). [ARN also stated that unauthorised entities are illegally selling internet over the Starlink network and that it will intensify enforcement](<https://arn.gw/comunicado-a-imprensa-fornecimento-ilegal-de-servicos-de-acesso-a-internet/>). No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Starlink went live in Equatorial Guinea on 29 August 2026, with an order page on starlink.com](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/08/31/starlink-is-live-in-equatorial-guinea/>), sold directly by Starlink under provisional approval. In the last twelve months, [Vice-president Nguema Obiang Mangue announced on 2026-09-09 that the country officially launched Starlink, operated by SpaceX](<https://agpgabon.ga/guinee-equatoriale-internet-satellitaire-starlink-officiellement-lance/>). [A government session that day placed legal selling authority with ORTEL and ordered individuals' contracts outside official channels cancelled](<https://ahoraeg.com/politica/2026/09/09/el-gobierno-exige-a-meta-tributar-en-guinea-ecuatorial-y-ordena-centralizar-la-comercializacion-de-starlink-en-ortel/>). No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Starlink is on sale in Kenya, with a capped plan priced at $10 a month in 2026](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/20/who-will-control-africas-satellite-internet-layer-starlink-amazon-leo-or-the-carriers/>). [Vodacom has a wholesale agreement with Starlink in Kenya](<https://www.telecomreviewafrica.com/articles/features/29151-the-rise-of-non-terrestrial-networks-integrating-leo-satellites-into-core-telecom-strategy/>). In the last twelve months, the Communications Authority of Kenya's count rose from [25,088 satellite internet subscriptions at 31 March 2026](<https://tech-ish.com/2026/06/19/starlink-hits-25000-subscribers-in-kenya/>) to [nearly 27,700 at 30 June 2026](<https://techtrendske.co.ke/2026/09/19/kenya-fixed-internet-fibre-wireless-satellite-growth/>). [Amazon Kuiper Kenya Limited has applied for a licence, and none is stated as granted](<https://techafricanews.com/2026/08/20/who-will-control-africas-satellite-internet-layer-starlink-amazon-leo-or-the-carriers/>). Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[MyBroadband's table of Starlink status in African countries, dated 17 July 2026, lists Liberia as 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). [Le360 lists Liberia among 29 African countries where Starlink had been granted a licence as of May 2026](<https://afrique.le360.ma/economie/internet-haut-debit-en-seulement-4-ans-starlink-operationnel-dans-un-pays-africain-sur-deux_UYXWC5RPWNGGFIYLU5VHL6L7ZU/>). [The LTA Board Chairman said Starlink has entered Liberia while the LTA drafts its first satellite regulations](<https://fpa.news/liberia-lta-unveils-sweeping-telecom-reforms-revokes-star-cell-license-after-six-years-of-inactivity/>). No change has been found in the last twelve months. No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[Eutelsat OneWeb is sold in Libya through a multi-year exclusive distribution agreement with a Libyan local partner, extended to LEO connectivity from early 2024](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/09/13/starlinks-libya-market-entry-remains-on-hold-as-negotiations-continue/>). It serves oil and gas, telecoms, finance, government and humanitarian customers. [Starlink is not licensed in Libya, and talks with the regulator GACI, open since 2024, had reached no agreement](<https://spaceinafrica.com/2026/09/13/starlinks-libya-market-entry-remains-on-hold-as-negotiations-continue/>). They were on hold until further notice as of the article's date. No change has been found in the last twelve months. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[MyBroadband's Starlink status table of 17 July 2026 lists Lesotho as 'Available'](<https://mybroadband.co.za/news/broadband/658586-starlink-launches-in-27th-african-country-before-south-africa.html>). In the last twelve months, [Vodacom Lesotho launched its Enterprise Satellite Connectivity solution in August 2026, a fully managed satellite broadband service powered by Starlink LEO](<https://www.thereporter.co.ls/2026/08/26/vodacom-launches-satellite-broadband-for-enterprises/>). [ITWeb Africa, citing Ookla, counts Lesotho among 27 African countries where Starlink is currently licensed, with no licence date given](<https://itweb.africa/article/starlink-drives-african-broadband-speeds-higher/GxwQD71DnGyvlPVo>). No source found says services on a second satellite network are on sale. Operating would need services on two different satellite networks on sale, such as Starlink and a OneWeb or Konnect service.

[The minister said customers without terrestrial broadband can get support for satellite internet under the VSAT initiative](<https://www.lavieeco.com/au-royaume/plan-national-du-haut-debit-un-taux-de-realisation-de-99-pour-la-premiere-phase/>), up to 2,500 dirhams per subscription from an approved provider.
